hook.line: Hey, I just wanted to share with you guys what AEO is.
hook.visual: A one-frame yellow cover card 'WHAT IS AEO?' with her waving hand, then a close webcam shot at her desk with a fixed 'What is AEO?' label and highlighted captions.

beats.what: Cover frame: big yellow 'WHAT IS AEO?' card while she waves at the camera.
Cut to a close desk shot; says she will define AEO for people hearing the term.
Recaps SEO as search engine optimization; aside about her dog chewing in the background.
Defines AEO as AI engine optimization.
Explains the shift: people used to 'just Google it', now they search differently.
Jump cut; names ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity as the new places people ask.
Jump cut; main point: what happened with SEO will soon happen with AEO.
Camera whips to the surfboard behind her to act out the 'ride the wave' line, then back.
Says businesses that do AEO will be a step ahead; invites comments.
Plugs her website by voice, then a black end frame with only the label.

characters.enters: Visible behind her the whole time as part of the set.
characters.acts: At the 'ride the wave' line she swings the camera onto it as a visual pun.
characters.exits: Camera swings back to her face.

why_it_works: The question in the hook stays on screen as a fixed label for the whole video, so anyone joining late knows the topic.
Plain-language definition by contrast with SEO, which the audience already knows.
Unpolished asides (dog chewing, 'so super cheesy') make her feel like a real person, not an ad.
Word-by-word captions with the current word boxed carry the video for sound-off viewers.
weaknesses: 104 s with 3 cuts and a 50 s longest shot; one definition is stretched to almost two minutes.
Almost all on-screen text (99.6%) sits outside the safe area, where TikTok's UI can cover it.
No proof or example of AEO in action; it is a definition only.
The CTA is spread over 'comment, reach out, check my site' with no single clear ask.
for_robert: Copy the prop pun: when Robert says a metaphor ('ride the wave'), cut to Fred acting it out in the scene for a second, then back; avoid her long single-take ramble.
